scenario: AITA for not jumping up and helping my parents bring in the groceries? I'm an adult and I pay rent if that helps. | I'm 33 years old and I've pretty much always lived with my parents. To me there's no shame in it because it's super cheap (they charge me $200, which honestly would be market rate where we live) and it has everything I want and need without the hassle of having to look for a new place to live. We get along most of the time but honestly I just avoid them. Recently the toilet flooded in my bathroom which means they are having to remodel my section of the house so we "run into" each other a lot more than when I used to lock myself in my room most of the time. Well today my parents went to Costco. When they got home I was sitting on the couch playing Apex and my mom asked me to get up and help them bring in groceries. I told her in a minute. I was honestly too into my game to notice that they made several trips back and forth and finally my dad told me to get my ass up. I told him I would in a minute. He said a minute is now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. It turned into a huge shouting match and now they are checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday (which is basically impossible). Of course they brought up my younger brother who is married with two kids and was just promoted at his job. They have their golden child of course but to throw his shit in my face is bullshit. I mean I guess I could have gotten up and helped them but to me because I pay rent that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole in this situation?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. I live with my parents, paying $200 rent, which is pretty cheap where we live. I've been living with them since I was pretty young, and mostly, we get along. But recently, there was a bathroom flood, so they had to remodel my section of the house, which means we're running into each other a lot more than before. I used to lock myself in my room most of the time, but now that's not possible. One day, my parents went to Costco. When they got home, I was sitting on the couch playing Apex Legends. My mom asked me to help bring in the groceries, and I told her I'd do it in a minute. I was really into the game and didn't notice that they made several trips back and forth. Finally, my dad told me to get my ass up, and I again said I'd do it in a minute. He got angry, grabbed the controller out of my hand, and it turned into a huge shouting match. Now, they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday, which is basically impossible. They also brought up my younger brother, who is married with two kids and just got promoted at his job. They're comparing me to him, which I find really unfair. I mean, I could have gotten up and helped them, but since I pay rent, I feel like I have the right to say no when they ask for help with things like groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole here? Alright, so to figure this out, I need to look at the situation from different angles. First, let's consider the dynamics of living with parents. I'm 33, which is an adult, and I'm paying rent, which is a responsibility. However, living with parents can sometimes lead to different expectations on both sides. My parents might expect more help around the house, especially since I'm living there, while I might feel that paying rent is sufficient. The incident with the groceries seems to be the tipping point. I was playing a game, and when my parents asked for help, I procrastinated. They ended up having to make multiple trips, which probably frustrated them. My dad got angry, and it escalated into a shouting match. Now, they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to find a place by Friday, which is a short timeframe. I also feel that they're comparing me to my younger brother, who is more successful in their eyes. This comparison is making me feel worse and adding to the conflict. I think I have a right to say no to helping with groceries or yard work because I'm paying rent, but maybe that's not the right way to look at it. On the other hand, living with others means there are shared responsibilities. Even though I'm paying rent, contributing to household chores is part of being a considerate housemate. My parents might feel that I'm not pulling my weight, especially since I'm an adult and they're expecting more from me. The fact that I was playing a game when they needed help might have made them feel that I'm not taking my responsibilities seriously. They might have felt disrespected when I kept saying I'd help in a minute but didn't follow through. This could have led to the shouting match and their decision to leave. Now, considering the comparison to my brother, it's clear that they have different expectations for each child. This can create resentment, especially if I feel that I'm being held to a higher standard or that my achievements aren't recognized. So, am I the asshole? Well, I didn't help when they asked, and I procrastinated, which led to their frustration. I also didn't handle the situation well when it escalated, which probably made things worse. However, I also feel that I'm contributing by paying rent, and I might expect some level of autonomy in how I spend my time. Maybe the key here is communication. If I had explained that I was in the middle of a game and would help as soon as I could, it might have diffused the situation. Instead, I kept saying I'd do it in a minute, which might have come off as dismissive. In the end, both sides have valid points. I need to consider my parents' feelings and the shared responsibilities of living together, while they need to understand that I'm an adult with my own life and responsibilities. Finding a balance might help prevent future conflicts. So, to answer the question: Am I the asshole? I think there's some asshole behavior on my part, like not helping when asked and not handling the conflict well. However, there's also asshole behavior from my parents in how they handled the situation and the unfair comparisons. It's a bit of both, but I need to take responsibility for my actions and work on communication to prevent this from happening again.
